entry.name: Merchant Payout Reconciler
entry.description: Prepares a private processor-transaction-to-payout reconciliation with separate bank-receipt evidence, preserving gross, fees, net, unsettled activity and failed payout attempts without moving funds or claiming settlement from arithmetic alone.
entry.audience: Merchant finance and payment-operations owners reconciling processor exports and bank receipt evidence for a bounded settlement period.
principles: Preserve transaction membership separately from payout status and bank receipt
Use supplied processor identities, signed amount conventions and currency scales
Keep unsettled transactions, failed attempts and every residual visible
boundaries: Do not infer payout membership from dates or matching amounts, especially for manual or instant payouts
Do not move funds, retry payouts, change bank details, release reserves, issue refunds, post accounting entries or contact processors
Do not decide fee legality, chargeback liability, reserve availability or accounting treatment
intake: Merchant and processor account aliases, one settlement currency and scale, report cutoff and timezone, source revisions, completeness assertions and private reviewer destination
Itemized processor balance transactions with native IDs, reporting categories, gross, signed fees, net and explicit payout membership or unsettled disposition
Payout records with stable attempt IDs, exact membership evidence, amounts, source-reported status and linked failed or returned attempts
Independent bank receipt rows and explicit owner mappings to payout attempts, retaining unmatched or ambiguous records
workflow: Bind the declared transaction and payout populations to current processor report scope and native identities
Reconcile row gross minus signed fee to net under the supplied convention, then reconcile member net amounts to each payout without re-subtracting fees
Partition every source transaction into exactly one current payout membership, unsettled record or unresolved membership question
Compare source payout status and independently mapped bank receipt evidence without treating expected arrival or a matched amount as receipt
Retain failed or returned attempts and retry lineage without double counting; prepare the private discrepancy workpaper and reviewer questions
deliverables: Independent bank receipt and failed-attempt comparison
Unsettled activity and private owner handoff

example.request: Reconcile synthetic payout P1 with a charge gross1000 fee30 net970, refund gross-100 fee0 net-100, and separate fee gross0 fee5 net-5; compare declared payout865 with bank receipt860 and retain a separate unsettled net194 transaction.
example.outcome: P1's member net is865 and its bank receipt residual is-5. Unsettled194 remains separate. Matching the processor payout does not clear the bank residual or settle the remaining transaction.

doneWhen: Every declared processor transaction, payout attempt and bank receipt has explicit coverage or an unresolved disposition
Each payout workpaper preserves row arithmetic, member-net comparison, bank receipt comparison and source status separately
Changed memberships, source revisions or receipt mappings invalidate prior review
The handoff contains no movement, accounting-close or settlement-certification claim
capabilityGuidance: X3 using minimized supplied exports only, with no payment-provider integration or execution authority.
Manual and instant payouts require supplied attributable membership evidence; unsupported or ambiguous reports stay blocked.

Write `outputs/merchant-payout-review.json` using `schemas/merchant-payout.schema.json` and `references/reconciliation-contract.md`, then the private Markdown handoff. Validate both schema and arithmetic; supplied completeness assertions are not independent source authentication.

contribution.problem: A net bank deposit does not explain which processor transactions, refunds and fees formed it, while a matching processor total does not establish receipt or settle remaining processor activity.
contribution.repeatableJob: Reconcile explicit processor transaction membership to payout amounts and independently supplied bank receipts while retaining unsettled transactions and failed payout attempts.
contribution.proofPlan: After admission: strict schema and semantics, exact signed minor-unit arithmetic, gross/fee/net conventions, membership conservation, duplicate native IDs, source cutoff and revision changes, standalone versus embedded fees, manual membership gaps, failed/returned/retry lineage and bank residual tests. Generated X3 Markdown workpaper, regression contract, current Control UI screenshot, full npm check and independent review. No live payment or settlement certification.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both compare supplied financial amounts, revisions and owner-controlled evidence before a handoff.
existingAlternatives.difference: Payroll compares employee/component registers and whole-period expectations. It does not partition processor balance transactions into payouts and unsettled activity, or track failed payout attempts versus bank receipts.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both preserve source-linked monetary transitions and unresolved review evidence.
existingAlternatives.difference: Construction pay applications reconcile cumulative work, stored materials and retainage, not processor transaction membership, payment fees or payout attempt lifecycle.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Matches source rows to statement transactions and preserves residuals and human authority.
existingAlternatives.difference: Can reconcile already-valued payout ledger entries to bank receipts. Its two-export account partition does not establish upstream processor membership, gross/fee/net decomposition, unsettled populations and failed payout attempt lineage. Reuse downstream rather than relabel bank matching as full settlement proof.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Conserves receipts and owner allocations while retaining unapplied cash.
existingAlternatives.difference: The receipt contract explicitly excludes inferred fees, netting and refunds. Customer receipt-to-invoice application is different from processor balance transactions grouped into settlement payouts.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Preserves return and refund evidence without executing a refund.
existingAlternatives.difference: Owns item return quantities, receipt and disposition; it does not reconcile processor payout batches or independently observed bank deposits.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Can prepare a source-preserving workbook with calculated amounts.
existingAlternatives.difference: Generic workbook integrity does not enforce transaction membership coverage, unsettled activity or payout-attempt versus bank-receipt states.
